liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hey Pocky Way** (2 reviews): This night's version was chosen for the So Many Roads 1965-1995 box set; Reviewer found Hey Pocky Way incredible [19][26]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Dew monstrous, and also praises the Terrapin into Hey Pocky Way; Reviewer says the Dew blew the crowd away [23][25]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Bobby opened the show, and the Hell In A Bucket was spirited for the year [19]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Terrapin titanic, within a short but massive second set [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Dancin' in the Street (5/11/86)**: back after 162 archived shows (725 days) [29]

## The recordings

- **gd89-03-31.schoeps-fob.childer.3826.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 182 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Schoeps FOB recording with plenty of audible crowd action; Track breaks are offbeat, and the tape includes unidentified filler [1][19]
- **gd1989-03-31.140966.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 21 songs; 151 min [2]
- **gd89-03-31.sbd.eD.16666.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 139 min; rated 4.29/5 by 16 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording captures the snug feel of the hall, with the band sounding tight [25]
- **gd1989-03-31.sbd.miller.32349.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 144 min; rated 3.69/5 by 16 [4]. Said about its sound: Level changes in Good Lovin' were fixed as best as possible [4]
- **gd1989-03-31.148151.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 150 min [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer camped on the grass around the coliseum and attended both nights of the Greensboro run [17]
- Traffic backed up badly outside, with far more cars than ticket holders; the reviewer's car overheated [20]
- Reviewer met Roscoe, who was taping for the first time at this show [20]
- Festival seating; fans waited in line a couple of hours and stood between Jerry and Brent at the railing [22]
- Lot scene had many Touch-heads and vendors who skipped the show, attracting local police [25]
- Reviewer needed a ticket and got help from a stranger outside [26]
- Packed crowd; at set break a group was hitting a bong about three feet tall [28]
- Reviewer sees this stretch of 1989 until Brent's death as a strong run where the band hit its stride [17]
- Roanoke, Hampton and Greensboro are named as the South's crown-jewel venues for Dead shows [21]
- On the first night, the reviewer stood about three rows back from Phil [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd89-03-31.schoeps-fob.childer.3826.sbeok.shnf**: source: schoeps cmc?/mk21> DAT fob [1]. Also: Schoeps mics, possibly CMC or MK21 capsules, to DAT, FOB; circulated via Childo and an unidentified seeder [1]
- **gd1989-03-31.140966.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck, Sony ESX-HiFi/L750 tape); Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics, ortf (OTS); Transfer Info: Master PCM… [2]. Also: Opening Hell In A Bucket > Sugaree and several short patches come from an AKG 414 BTL mics source [2]
- **gd89-03-31.sbd.eD.16666.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd>cass>dat>cd>eac>wav>shn>wav>shn [3]
- **gd1989-03-31.sbd.miller.32349.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat (44.1k) D [4]. Also: One track was patched from soundboard to master cassette, then 20-bit Sonic, then CD [4]
- **gd1989-03-31.148151.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [5]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [5]
